Dated : 4th November, 2025 This is a petition filed by the accused in C.P.No.88/2023 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Mavelikkara, arising out of crime No.444/2023 of Kurathikadu police station under Section 482 Cr.P.C praying for quashing all further proceedings against him.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Mavelikkara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 366, 342, 324, 323, 376,
376(2)(n), 354(a) (b)
(d) IPC and Section 67A of the Information and Technology Act (IT Act).

2. The prosecution case is that the accused who is the friend of the husband of the de facto complainant with the intention to satisfy his sexual lust, made friendship with the de facto complainant and on 8.5.2023 at 8.00 pm took her in a motor cycle to the bed room of his residence,
locked the door from inside and tried to molest her.

When she resisted, the accused assaulted her,
committed rape upon her, took her nude photographs, sent the same into the WhatsApp of CW1,
intimidated her and continued the relationship till 29.6.2023, after promissing to marry her and thereby he alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
3.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, it is a false case foisted against him.

Further,
according to the learned counsel, even as per the allegations raised against the petitioner, it was only a consensual relationship and therefore, according to him, continuance of the proceedings 2025:KER:83188 against the petitioner is only an abuse of the process of the Court.

Further,
according to the leaned counsel, the matter has been settled with the de facto complainant and she filed an affidavit supporting the factum of settlement.

4. The learned Public Prosecutor, after getting instruction from the investigating officer also submitted that the dispute has been settled between the parties and that the victim is not at all interested in continuing the prosecution against the petitioner.

5. On a perusal of the F.I. statement, it can be seen that on 9.5.2023 at about 8.00 pm the de facto complainant went along with the petitioner in his motor cycle to his residence and on that day at about 9.00 pm he committed rape upon her.
Thereafter, he dropped her at her residence at about 11.00 pm.
The reason given by her in the FI statement for not reporting the matter to the police is that the petitioner agreed to marry her within two days.

The above reason given by the de facto complainant that the petitioner agreed to marry her within two days and that is why she did not report the matter to the police cannot be true as at the time of the incident, she was already married and not competent to contract another marriage.
From the F.I. statement, it appears that the relationship continued during several subsequent days and according to her, it was again on the basis of a promise of marriage given by the petitioner.

Since the de facto complainant was already married and incompetent to contract another marriage, the claim of the de facto complainant that she had consented 2025:KER:83188 to the relationship in the light of promise of marriage, cannot be believed.

In other words, it is to be held that the relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant was a consensual one and as such, no purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioner.
Further, now the matter has been settled between the parties.
On that account also, further proceedings in the case will not yield any fruitful result.

6. Considering the fact that the offences involved in this case are not purely of private in nature and now the dispute has been settled between the parties, this is a fit case in which further proceedings can be quashed by invoking the inherent power of this court.
Such a course is also required to maintain harmonious relationship between the parties and also to prevent abuse of process of the court.
In the result, this Crl. M.C is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in C.P.No.88/2023 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Mavelikkara arising from Crime No.444/2023 of Kurathikadu police station, is quashed.
